RT by @hey_itsmyturn: FACT CHECK: Misleading “proof of life.” RT and other outlets presented footage released on August 8 as rare images of Mojtaba Khamenei. But the same undated classroom video was already broadcast on March 19–20. There is another problem: Iranian media reported in September 2024 that Khamenei had suspended this seminary class. If the footage shows those lessons, it likely predates that announcement and could be nearly two years old. Mehr provided no recording date, location, participant names or explanation for recycling it now. There is no evidence the video is fabricated, but nothing proves it is recent either. After five months without a verified public appearance, old classroom footage is not proof of his present condition. It looks more like carefully timed proof-of-life theatre.

RT by @hey_itsmyturn: 🇺🇸 Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says pipelines could divert 50–70% of Hormuz energy traffic within two years, making the strait almost “irrelevant.” Existing bypasses: • Saudi East–West pipeline: Persian Gulf fields → Yanbu on the Red Sea, rated at 7 million barrels/day. Actual exports are constrained by refineries, storage and Yanbu’s loading terminals. • UAE Habshan–Fujairah pipeline: Abu Dhabi → Gulf of Oman, about 1.8 million bpd. A second line planned for 2027 could raise combined capacity to roughly 3.6 million. • Iran’s Goreh–Jask pipeline: Iranian fields → Gulf of Oman, but effective capacity is only about 300,000 bpd. • Iraq–Türkiye pipeline: Kirkuk → Ceyhan, currently carrying a fraction of its 1.5 million-bpd theoretical capacity. Extending it to southern Iraq remains a proposal, not finished infrastructure. Hormuz previously carried nearly 20 million bpd of oil. The IEA estimates today’s genuinely available bypass capacity at only 3.5–5.5 million bpd. Diverting 50–70% would require roughly 10–14 million bpd, plus new pumping stations, storage tanks and export terminals. The biggest flaw is LNG: Qatar ships around 9.3 billion cubic feet per day through Hormuz. LNG cannot simply be pumped through an oil pipeline. A replacement would require enormous gas pipelines across several countries or entirely new liquefaction and export terminals outside the Gulf. Reducing dependence on Hormuz is possible. Making it irrelevant by 2028 is not a construction plan yet. It is a political prediction with a very large engineering gap.

RT by @leventkemaI: The Makkah Joint Defense Agreement reflects the depth and longstanding nature of the strategic relations among the three countries, which have developed over several decades, and represents the culmination of detailed negotiations conducted over a number of years. The Makkah Joint Defense Agreement enables the three signatory countries to develop joint defense capabilities, strengthen strategic deterrence, enhance readiness, and further develop and integrate their respective defense capabilities to jointly address any threats to their safety and security. Under the agreement, any external armed attack against any one of the three countries shall be regarded as an attack against all three. The agreement does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc. Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race, rather it is focused on building sustainable capabilities. The agreement does not come at the expense of the Kingdom’s strong and strategic relations with its Gulf, Arab, and international partners. It does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states. The agreement does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries, or between them and other states or international organizations.
